title: Distinct indices in an AND-clause
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $lits$ be a list of Boolean-circuit literals on $n$ variables whose variable indices are pairwise distinct. If an AND circuit $c$ equals the base clause constructed from $lits$ and this distinctness condition, then the variable indices in $lits$ are pairwise distinct.
hypotheses_covered: The variable indices in $lits$ are pairwise distinct
The AND circuit $c$ equals the base clause constructed from $lits$ and the distinctness witness
replaced:
Fix $n$, and let $lits$ be a list of literals over the variables $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$ whose
underlying variable indices, obtained by taking the index of each literal in $lits$, are
pairwise distinct. If a normal-form AND circuit on $n$ variables equals the base clause
built from $lits$ together with this distinctness witness, then the list of variable
indices of $lits$ has no repeated entries.
